newsitem.title: FRANCE: Shippers say no confirmation of Iraq wheat deals.
newsitem.headline: Shippers say no confirmation of Iraq wheat deals.

text.p: French grain traders were trying to get to the bottom of market speculation that Iraq had bought more wheat from France but exporters stressed on Thursday there was no confirmation of any deals so far.

French wheat prices gained a little support from speculation that Baghdad had bought some 200,000 tonnes of French wheat at a delivered price at or below $190 per tonne -- described by French traders as very aggressive if it turns to be true.
But exporters said there was no word from Baghdad on its tender for 100,000 tonnes of French wheat, launched this week.

The picture was further clouded by comments from Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz, who said during a visit to France on Wednesday that Iraq had signed contracts with three French companies for 100,000 tonnes each of wheat.
Iraq was reported to have bought 300,000 tonnes of French wheat in December, a figure which was later reduced to 200,000.
Aziz did not say whether he was referring to contracts signed in December or the new negotiations under way this week.
Traders said there was also unconfirmed talk that Iraq had bought Argentine wheat.
Iraq is buying wheat with money raised from oil sales under a six-month humanitarian relief pact with the United Nations.
At France's northern port of Rouen, delivered soft wheat was quoted at 857.50 francs a tonne excluding carrying charges on Thursday, up slightly from 855.00 francs on Wednesday.
"There are few sellers around today," said one broker.
